examples.en: In the movie, the hero punishes the bad guys.
He got angry and said he would make the lying friend pay.

examples.ko: 소비자들이 불매 운동으로 그 회사를 응징했어요.
examples.en: Consumers punished the company with a boycott.

examples.ko: 잘못을 응징하기보다 이유를 들어 보려고 했어요.
examples.en: Rather than punish the mistake, I tried to hear the reason.

examples.ko: 약속을 어긴 친구를 응징하고 싶었지만 참았어요.
examples.en: I wanted to get back at the friend who broke the promise, but I held back.
The customers punished the unkind shop with their star ratings.

explain: '혼내다'가 가까운 사람을 꾸짖는 말이라면 '응징하다'는 잘못에 대해 따끔하게 갚아 준다는 느낌이 강하고 조금 무거운 말이에요. 부모가 아이를 혼낼 때는 쓰지 않아요. 주로 영화, 뉴스, 글에 나와요.

phrases.example: 나쁜 짓을 한 사람은 응징을 받아야 해요.
phrases.en: People who do bad things should be punished.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '응징'과 함께 벌을 받는 쪽에서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the noun 응징, said from the side of the one receiving the punishment.

phrases.example: 저는 거짓말한 그 사람을 응징하고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to make that liar pay.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람을 나타내는 연결형으로, 강한 분노를 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form expressing a wish, showing strong anger.

phrases.en: The hero sharply punished the villain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '따끔하게'를 붙여서 잘못을 단단히 갚아 준다는 느낌을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 따끔하게 stresses paying back a wrong sharply.

explain_en: While '혼내다' is scolding someone close to you, '응징하다' feels heavier, like making someone pay sharply for a wrong. Parents do not use it for scolding children. It mostly appears in movies, news and writing.

examples.en: My uncle joined that party last year.

examples.ko: 정치에 관심이 생겨서 이번에 입당하려고 해요.
examples.en: I've become interested in politics, so I'm going to join a party this time.
If you join the party, you have to pay membership dues.

examples.ko: 유명 배우가 여당에 입당한다는 소문이 돌아요.
examples.en: There's a rumor going around that a famous actor will join the ruling party.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 입당하지 않고 무소속으로 나왔어요.
examples.en: He didn't join a party and ran as an independent.
What made you decide to join the party?

explain: '정당에 입당하다'처럼 '~에'와 함께 쓰고, 정당에만 써요. 동아리나 회사, 모임에 들어갈 때는 '가입하다'를 써요. 반대말은 '탈당하다'예요.

phrases.example: 그는 입당 원서를 내고 정식 당원이 됐어요.
phrases.en: He submitted his party application and became an official member.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정당에 들어가기 위해 서류를 제출하는 절차를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes submitting the paperwork to join a political party.

phrases.en: My friend invited me to join the party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '입당'을 써서 정당에 들어오라고 권할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 입당 to say someone recommends joining a party.
phrases.en_equiv: to invite (someone) to join a party

phrases.en: I haven't joined any political party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로, 정당에 가입하지 않은 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, stating that one is not a member of any party.

explain_en: It is used with '~에', as in '정당에 입당하다', and only for political parties. For clubs, companies or groups, you use '가입하다' instead. The opposite is '탈당하다' (to leave a party).

examples.en: The National Assembly belongs to the legislative branch.
The legislative branch is the place that makes laws.

examples.ko: 삼권 분립은 입법부, 행정부, 사법부로 나뉘어요.
examples.en: The separation of powers is divided into legislative, executive and judicial branches.
The legislature passed a new law.
The president must respect the legislature's decisions.
A conflict arose between the legislature and the executive.

explain: 입법부는 뉴스와 사회 교과서에서 쓰는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '국회'라고 하는 경우가 훨씬 많아요. 나라 일을 나누어 맡는 세 곳을 '입법부·행정부·사법부'라고 한꺼번에 묶어서 외워 두세요.

phrases.example: 입법부와 행정부는 서로 하는 일이 달라요.
phrases.en: The legislature and the executive branch do different jobs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라 일을 나누어 맡는 곳을 함께 말할 때 자주 묶어서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired when talking about the branches that share the work of government.

phrases.en: A country is divided into legislative, executive, and judicial branches.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세 곳을 한꺼번에 말하는 표현이라서 교과서나 뉴스에서 잘 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names all three branches together; common in textbooks and news.

phrases.en: Laws are made in the National Assembly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입법부는 딱딱한 말이고, 일상에서는 '국회'라고 훨씬 많이 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 입법부 is formal; in daily life people say 국회 much more often.

explain_en: 입법부 is a word from news and social studies textbooks. In daily life people say '국회' much more often. Remember the three branches together: '입법부·행정부·사법부'.

examples.en: The enlistment notice came to my house.
My enlistment date has been set, so my feelings are mixed.

examples.ko: 입영을 앞두고 친구들이 송별회를 열어 줬어요.
examples.en: With my enlistment coming up, my friends threw me a farewell party.
I want to go on a trip before enlisting.
I decided to take time off school because of my enlistment.

examples.ko: 입영 연기를 신청하려면 어떻게 해야 해요?
examples.en: What do I have to do to apply to postpone enlistment?

explain: '입영 통지서', '입영 날짜', '입영 연기'처럼 합쳐서 자주 써요. 일상에서는 '군대 가다'가 더 흔하고, 같은 상황에서 '입대'라는 말도 써요. 군대를 마치고 나오는 것은 '제대'나 '전역'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I got my enlistment notice yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입영 날짜와 장소가 적힌 공식 문서를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the official document that gives the enlistment date and place.

phrases.en: I applied to postpone my enlistment because of school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입영 날짜를 뒤로 미루는 것을 말하고 공식적인 자리에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means putting off the enlistment date; used in formal settings.

phrases.en: My friend is going into the army next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입영보다 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자주 쓰는 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A much more common, casual way to say this in everyday conversation.

explain_en: It appears in compounds like '입영 통지서', '입영 날짜' and '입영 연기'. In daily talk '군대 가다' is more common, and '입대' is also used for the same situation. Finishing service is called '제대' or '전역'.

examples.en: The troops kept training even in the cold weather.
Citizens wrote letters for the soldiers.
The news said the meals for soldiers have gotten better.
A soldier on leave is waiting for the bus.

examples.ko: 이 공연은 장병과 가족을 위한 무대예요.
examples.en: This show is a stage for soldiers and their families.

examples.ko: 병원은 아픈 장병에게 먼저 치료를 해 줬어요.
examples.en: The hospital treated the sick soldiers first.

explain: 장교(간부)와 병사를 함께 묶어 부르는 말이에요. 뉴스나 공식 발표에서 많이 쓰고, 보통은 '군인'이라고 해요. 한 사람을 가리킬 때보다 '장병들'처럼 여럿을 가리킬 때가 많아요.

phrases.en: I wrote a thank-you letter to the soldiers of the Korean armed forces.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 공식 자리에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in news and formal settings.

phrases.en: The soldiers are training in the snow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '장병'보다 '군인'을 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life, 군인 is used much more than 장병.

phrases.en: The troops are training hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-들'을 붙여 여러 명을 한꺼번에 가리킬 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -들, it commonly refers to a group of service members.

explain_en: It groups officers and enlisted soldiers together. It is common in news and official announcements; in daily talk people just say '군인'. It is usually used for groups, as in '장병들'.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 정보기관 요원의 이야기를 다뤄요.
examples.en: That movie deals with the story of an intelligence agent.
Data released by the intelligence agency was on the news.
Each country runs its own intelligence agency.

examples.ko: 그는 정보기관에서 십 년 넘게 일했어요.
examples.en: He worked at an intelligence agency for over ten years.

examples.ko: 정보기관은 보통 하는 일을 공개하지 않아요.
examples.en: Intelligence agencies usually don't disclose their work.
I wonder whether we can trust the intelligence agency's announcement.

explain: 나라의 안전을 위해 정보를 모으고 분석하는 기관을 말해요. 뉴스나 영화에서 자주 나오고, 보통 '국가정보원' 같은 구체적인 이름 대신 일반적으로 부를 때 써요.

phrases.en: The main character of that drama is an intelligence agent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 드라마에서 자주 듣는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often heard in movies and dramas.

phrases.en: Everyone is waiting for the intelligence agency's announcement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 기관이 한 말을 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in news when reporting what the agency said.

phrases.en: A national intelligence agency protects the nation's safety.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라에서 운영하는 기관임을 분명히 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clear it is run by the state.

explain_en: It refers to an agency that gathers and analyzes information for national security. It appears in news and films, and is used as a general term instead of a specific name such as '국가정보원'.

examples.en: Political awareness among young people has risen.

examples.ko: 정치의식을 키우려면 뉴스를 꾸준히 봐야 해요.
examples.en: To build political awareness, you need to watch the news steadily.
Political awareness grows through education too.

examples.ko: 이 수업은 학생들의 정치의식에 큰 영향을 줬어요.
examples.en: This class had a big effect on the students' political awareness.
We need healthy political awareness and a sense of responsibility.
When political awareness is low, the voting rate drops too.

explain: 정치와 사회 문제에 관심을 갖고 자기 생각을 가지는 태도를 말해요. '정치의식이 높다/낮다/강하다'처럼 정도를 나타내는 말과 자주 함께 써요. 뉴스, 토론, 사회 수업에서 많이 나오는 표현이에요.

phrases.en: University students these days have high political awareness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관심이 많고 생각이 뚜렷하다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means having strong interest and clear views.

phrases.example: 투표율이 낮으면 정치의식이 낮다고 말하기도 해요.
phrases.en: When the voting rate is low, people sometimes say political awareness is low.
phrases.nuance_ko: '높다'와 반대로 관심이 적을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 높다, used when interest is low.

phrases.example: 토론 수업이 정치의식을 키우는 데 도움이 돼요.
phrases.en: Debate class helps build political awareness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교육이나 활동으로 관심을 높일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when raising awareness through education or activities.

explain_en: It describes the attitude of paying attention to politics and social issues and holding your own views. It often goes with words of degree, such as '정치의식이 높다/낮다/강하다'. You will see it a lot in news, debates and social studies classes.

examples.en: I was left off this list.
Children are excluded from the discount.
That item was dropped from the meeting agenda.
The injured player will be left out of the game.
Please make sure nobody is left out.

examples.ko: 저만 계획에서 제외된 것 같아서 서운해요.
examples.en: I feel hurt because it seems only I was left out of the plan.

explain: '에서'와 함께 '명단에서 제외되다'처럼 어디서 빠졌는지를 같이 말해요. 사람이 빠지면 기분이 상하는 느낌이 있고, 안내문에서는 명사 '제외'만 써서 '○○ 제외'라고도 해요. 반대말은 '포함되다'예요.

phrases.en: My name was left out of the list.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제외되다'보다 쉬운 일상 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, everyday expression.

phrases.en: This price excludes tax.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빼는 쪽이 주어가 되는 능동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, where the one excluding is the subject.

phrases.en: Breakfast is included in the room rate.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제외되다'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 제외되다.

explain_en: Pair it with 에서 to say what you were dropped from, like 명단에서 제외되다. When a person is the one left out it can carry a hurt feeling. On notices you will also see the bare noun, like '○○ 제외'. The opposite is 포함되다.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 오십 년째 존속하고 있어요.
examples.en: That shop has continued to exist for fifty years.
This system will continue to exist in the future too.
For the company to survive, new investment is needed.
That organization survived even during the war.

examples.ko: 오래 존속해 온 전통을 지키고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to protect a tradition that has lasted a long time.
It is hard for the theater to survive this way.

explain: 비슷한 '유지하다'는 사람이 애써서 지킬 때 쓰고, '존속하다'는 회사·제도·단체가 사라지지 않고 이어질 때 써요. 주어가 사람이 아닌 경우가 대부분이에요. 뉴스나 글에서 많이 보여요.

phrases.en: If customers decrease, it is hard for the shop to continue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속 이어 가기 힘들 때 쓰는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used when it is hard to keep something going.

phrases.example: 그 회사의 존속 기간은 삼십 년이었어요.
phrases.en: That company lasted for thirty years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사라지지 않고 이어진 기간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the length of time something kept existing.

phrases.en: The tradition of that shop has continued until now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '존속하다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more common in daily speech than '존속하다'.

explain_en: '유지하다' is for something a person works to keep going, while '존속하다' is for a company, system, or group that does not disappear and carries on. The subject is almost never a person. You see it often in news and writing.

dis.h: formal; keep existing, like an institution

p.s: 그 단체는 백 년 넘게 존속하고 있다.
p.o: 그 단체는 백 년 넘게 계속되고 있다.
p.n: 계속되다 says it keeps going; 존속하다 says it still exists.

examples.en: The government drafted young men in preparation for war.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 농민들을 징집해서 성을 쌓게 했대요.
examples.en: I heard that in the old days, farmers were conscripted to build castles.
The army came to the village to conscript the people.

examples.ko: 나라가 청년을 징집하면 가족들은 큰 걱정에 빠져요.
examples.en: When a country drafts its young men, their families fall into deep worry.

examples.ko: 인원을 더 징집해야 한다는 의견이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Some voiced the opinion that more people should be drafted.

examples.ko: 징집하는 기준이 너무 불공평하다는 비판이 있어요.
examples.en: There is criticism that the criteria for conscription are too unfair.

explain: 주어가 나라나 군대일 때 쓰고, 불려 가는 쪽에서는 '징집되다'나 '입대하다'라고 말해요. 일상 대화보다는 역사 수업이나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 청년은 전쟁 때 군대에 징집됐어요.
phrases.en: That young man was drafted into the army during the war.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불려 가는 사람 입장에서 말할 때 쓰는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, used from the viewpoint of the person being called up.

phrases.en: The country conscripted farmers as soldiers.
phrases.nuance_ko: '군인으로'를 붙이면 무엇으로 불러 모으는지가 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '군인으로' makes clear what people are being called up as.

phrases.en: That country does not conscript women.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않다'를 붙인 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form made with '-지 않다'.

explain_en: It is used when the subject is a state or army, and from the side of those being called up, people say '징집되다' or '입대하다'. It appears more in history classes and the news than in everyday talk.

examples.ko: 여성의 참정권은 오랜 노력 끝에 얻어졌어요.
examples.en: Women's right to take part in politics was won after long effort.
You have the right to vote from age 18.

examples.ko: 재외 국민도 참정권을 행사할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Citizens living abroad can also exercise their voting rights.
We learned the history of political participation rights in social studies.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 외국인에게도 지방 선거 참정권을 줘요.
examples.en: That country gives foreigners the right to vote in local elections too.

examples.ko: 참정권을 요구하는 시위가 백 년 전에 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a protest demanding the right to vote a hundred years ago.

explain: 일상에서 투표할 권리는 보통 '투표권'이라고 해요. '참정권'은 투표하는 권리뿐 아니라 선거에 나갈 권리까지 포함하는 더 넓은 말이라 사회 수업이나 뉴스에서 많이 나와요. '참정권을 얻다', '참정권을 행사하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I exercised my right to vote at the election.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가진 권리를 실제로 사용한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means actually using the right one holds.

phrases.en: That country gave suffrage to women as well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라나 법이 권리를 인정해 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a country or law grants the right.

phrases.en: You get the right to vote at age 18.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 투표할 권리를 이 말로 더 자주 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday speech this is the more common word for the right to vote.

explain_en: In daily life people usually say '투표권' for the right to vote. '참정권' is broader, covering both voting and the right to run in elections, and appears in social studies and the news. Typical phrases are '참정권을 얻다' and '참정권을 행사하다'.

examples.en: The government promised to root out corruption.

examples.ko: 새 시장은 오랜 비리 척결 의지를 밝혔어요.
examples.en: The new mayor stated his resolve to eliminate long-standing irregularities.
It's an old problem that is not easy to eliminate.

examples.ko: 척결 대상이 된 관행을 두고 논란이 많아요.
examples.en: There is much debate over the practice that became a target for elimination.
Slogans alone can't eradicate illegal practices.

examples.ko: 시민들은 쓰레기 불법 투기 척결에 힘을 모았어요.
examples.en: Citizens joined forces to stop illegal dumping.

explain: 뉴스나 연설에서 '부정부패 척결', '비리 척결'처럼 나쁜 것을 뿌리째 없앤다는 강한 느낌으로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '없애다'를 쓰고, 대상은 보통 사람이 아니라 비리, 관행, 악습 같은 것이에요.

phrases.en: Citizens started a campaign to root out corruption.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 것을 없애자고 여럿이 함께 하는 활동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An activity in which many people work together to get rid of something bad.

phrases.en: Old bad practices are also targets for elimination.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반드시 없애야 할 문제를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for problems that must be eliminated.

phrases.example: 학교 폭력 근절을 위해 새 법이 만들어졌어요.
phrases.en: A new law was made to stamp out school violence.
phrases.nuance_ko: '척결'과 비슷하게 뿌리째 없앤다는 뜻으로 뉴스에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '척결', used in the news to mean getting rid of something at its root.

explain_en: In news and speeches it appears in phrases like '부정부패 척결' with a strong sense of wiping out something bad at its root. In daily conversation people say '없애다'. The target is usually things like corruption, practices or bad customs, not people.

examples.en: The government decided to abolish the outdated regulations.
The company did away with unnecessary rules.
The school plans to eliminate the complicated procedures.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 관세를 철폐하는 데 합의했어요.
examples.en: The two countries agreed to eliminate tariffs.
The voices calling for an end to discrimination grew louder.

examples.ko: 옛 제도를 철폐하고 새 방식을 도입했어요.
examples.en: They abolished the old system and introduced a new method.

explain: '규제를 철폐하다', '차별을 철폐하다'처럼 목적어가 제도, 규제, 장벽, 차별이에요. 사람이 쓰는 물건이나 일상의 일에는 쓰지 않아요. 일상에서 비슷한 상황은 '없애다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The company got rid of the old rule.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '철폐하다' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday substitute for 철폐하다.

phrases.en: Unfair discrimination must be abolished.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼭 없애야 한다는 주장을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to argue that something must be done away with.

phrases.en: He argues that this system should be abolished.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-자고 주장하다'로 의견을 전하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Reports someone's opinion using -자고 주장하다.

explain_en: The object is a system, regulation, barrier or discrimination, as in '규제를 철폐하다' or '차별을 철폐하다'. It is not used for ordinary objects or daily matters, where people just say '없애다'.

en: being newly-elected; being elected for the first time

examples.ko: 이번 선거에서 초선 의원이 많이 당선됐어요.
examples.en: Many first-term lawmakers were elected in this election.

examples.ko: 그분은 초선이지만 활동을 정말 열심히 해요.
examples.en: She is in her first term, but she works really hard.

examples.ko: 초선 때는 모든 일이 낯설었다고 말했어요.
examples.en: He said everything felt unfamiliar during his first term.
I cheered on my junior who entered the National Assembly as a first-term member.

examples.ko: 우리 지역 초선 시장이 새 정책을 발표했어요.
examples.en: The first-term mayor of our area announced a new policy.

examples.ko: 토론회에는 초선과 다선 의원이 함께 나왔어요.
examples.en: First-term and veteran lawmakers appeared together at the debate.

explain: 두 번째로 당선되면 '재선', 여러 번이면 '다선'이라고 해요. 국회의원, 시장 같은 선거로 뽑는 자리에 쓰고, 선거 뉴스에서 '초선 의원'이라는 말로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The first-term lawmakers gathered and held a meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음 당선된 의원을 부르는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for a legislator in their first term.

phrases.en: He was elected for the first time last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음으로 선거에서 뽑혔다는 뜻으로 '으로'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means being elected for the first time; used with the particle 으로.
phrases.en_equiv: to be elected for the first time

phrases.en: The mayor succeeded in being re-elected in this election.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 번째로 당선되는 것을 말해요. '초선' 다음 단계예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means winning a second election; it comes after 초선.

explain_en: Being elected a second time is '재선', and being elected many times is '다선'. It is used for elected posts such as lawmakers and mayors, and often appears in election news as '초선 의원'.

en: to infringe on; to violate (rights, privacy)

examples.ko: 개인 정보를 침해하면 법으로 처벌받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you infringe on someone's personal information, you can be punished by law.
Don't invade other people's privacy.
The company infringed on its employees' rights.

examples.ko: 이 광고는 저작권을 침해한 것으로 보여요.
examples.en: This ad looks like it infringes on a copyright.

examples.ko: 사진을 마음대로 올리는 건 초상권을 침해하는 일이에요.
examples.en: Posting photos without permission violates image rights.
There was a problem because we encroached on the neighbor's land.

explain: '침해하다'는 권리, 사생활, 저작권처럼 법과 약속으로 지켜지는 것에만 써요. '방해하다'는 하던 일을 못 하게 막을 때, '침해하다'는 넘으면 안 되는 선을 넘어 들어갈 때 써요. 일상 대화보다 뉴스와 법 이야기에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.example: 다른 사람의 사진을 쓰면 저작권을 침해할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you use someone else's photo, you may infringe copyright.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법으로 지켜지는 권리와 함께 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing with a legally protected right.

phrases.en: I got angry because my privacy was violated.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권리를 빼앗긴 사람 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person whose rights were violated.

phrases.en: This is clearly a violation of rights.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사로 쓰면 뉴스나 법 이야기에서 더 딱딱하고 분명하게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a noun it sounds firmer, as in news or legal talk.

explain_en: Use it only for things protected by law or agreement, such as rights, privacy, and copyright. 방해하다 is for getting in the way of an activity, while 침해하다 is for crossing a line into someone's protected space. You hear it more in news and legal talk than in daily conversation.

examples.ko: 국제 사회는 테러리즘에 함께 대응하고 있어요.
examples.en: The international community is responding to terrorism together.
They held a discussion on counter-terrorism measures on the news.

examples.ko: 테러리즘을 막기 위해 공항 검색이 강화됐어요.
examples.en: Airport screening was tightened to prevent terrorism.

examples.ko: 이 책은 테러리즘의 역사를 다루고 있어요.
examples.en: This book deals with the history of terrorism.

examples.ko: 테러리즘이 세계 평화를 위협한다는 기사를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read an article saying terrorism threatens world peace.

examples.ko: 테러리즘은 어떤 이유로도 정당화될 수 없어요.
examples.en: Terrorism cannot be justified for any reason.

explain: 일상에서는 보통 '테러'라고 짧게 말하고, '테러리즘'은 뉴스, 수업, 글에서 그런 행위나 이념 전체를 말할 때 써요. 사람은 '테러리스트'라고 해요. 뉴스에서는 '테러리즘 대응', '반테러'처럼 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: A terror attack almost happened at the airport.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '테러리즘'보다 '테러'를 더 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech 테러 is used more than 테러리즘.

phrases.en: The police caught a terrorist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 테러를 일으키는 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who carries out terrorism.

phrases.en: Several countries strengthened anti-terror cooperation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 '반테러 협력', '반테러 정책'처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Seen in the news in phrases like anti-terror cooperation or policy.

explain_en: In everyday speech people usually just say '테러', while '테러리즘' appears in news, classes and writing when talking about the practice or ideology as a whole. A person is called a '테러리스트'. In the news you often see phrases like '테러리즘 대응' and '반테러'.

en: to dismiss from office; to remove from a post

examples.en: The city hall dismissed the employee who committed corruption.
The committee decided to dismiss that public official.

examples.ko: 규칙을 어긴 교사를 파면했다는 기사를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read an article saying a teacher who broke the rules was dismissed.
If someone is dismissed, their pension can be reduced too.
The disciplinary committee is discussing whether to dismiss or suspend.

examples.ko: 기관장이 직원을 파면한 것은 부당하다고 주장해요.
examples.en: They claim it was unjust for the head of the agency to dismiss the employee.

explain: 회사에서 내보낼 때는 보통 '해고하다'라고 하고, '파면하다'는 공무원·교원 같은 공직에서 징계로 쫓아낼 때 써요. 같은 징계라도 '해임'보다 더 무거운 처분으로 알려져 있어요. 일상 대화보다는 뉴스에서 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: That teacher was dismissed after disciplinary action.
phrases.nuance_ko: 파면을 당하는 쪽에서 말하는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, said from the side of the person dismissed.

phrases.en: That official received a dismissal order.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식적으로 내려지는 징계를 말할 때 '처분'과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '처분' for an official disciplinary decision.

phrases.en: The company fired an employee who broke the rules.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사에서 내보낼 때는 '파면하다' 대신 이 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this instead of 파면하다 when a company lets someone go.

explain_en: When a company lets someone go, people usually say '해고하다'; '파면하다' is for removing someone from a public post, such as a civil servant or teacher, as discipline. It is known as a heavier penalty than '해임'. You hear it more in the news than in everyday conversation.

examples.en: The constitution guarantees the right to equality of all citizens.

examples.ko: 그 규정은 평등권에 어긋난다는 의견이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people say that rule goes against the right to equality.

examples.ko: 평등권은 사람이면 누구나 가지는 기본적인 권리예요.
examples.en: The right to equality is a basic right that every person has.

examples.ko: 장애인의 평등권을 지키기 위한 법이 만들어졌어요.
examples.en: A law was made to protect the equal rights of people with disabilities.
Equal rights issues often appear in the news.

examples.ko: 이 단체는 이주민의 평등권을 위해 활동해요.
examples.en: This group works for the equal rights of immigrants.

explain: '평등'은 일반적인 말이고, '평등권'은 법에서 보장하는 권리라는 느낌이에요. 보통 '평등권을 보장하다/침해하다/지키다'처럼 써요. 뉴스, 법, 사회 수업에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 법은 여성의 평등권을 침해한다는 비판을 받았어요.
phrases.en: That law was criticized for violating women's right to equality.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권리가 지켜지지 않았다고 말하는 뉴스나 법 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in news and legal talk when a right has been violated.
phrases.en_equiv: to violate the right to equality

phrases.example: 모두의 평등권을 지키기 위해 법을 고쳤어요.
phrases.en: They revised the law to protect everyone's right to equality.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권리를 보호한다는 긍정적인 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has the positive sense of protecting a right.
phrases.en_equiv: to protect the right to equality

phrases.en: Guaranteeing equal rights is the foundation of a democratic society.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사형으로 제목이나 글에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This noun form often appears in headlines and writing.

explain_en: '평등' (equality) is the general word, while '평등권' feels like a legally guaranteed right. It is usually used as '평등권을 보장하다/침해하다/지키다'. It appears often in news, law and social studies classes.

examples.en: An angry customer assaulted an employee.
People nearby stopped the person who was about to attack someone.
If you assault someone, you are punished by law.

examples.ko: 친구를 폭행한 학생이 학교에서 징계를 받았어요.
examples.en: The student who assaulted a friend was disciplined by the school.

examples.ko: 아이를 폭행하는 일은 절대 있어서는 안 돼요.
examples.en: Hitting a child must never happen.
He assaulted a coworker and lost his job.

explain: '폭행하다'는 사람을 때리거나 힘으로 해치는 행동에 써요. 뉴스와 법 이야기에서 자주 나오는 딱딱한 말이라 일상 대화에서는 '때리다'가 더 자연스러워요. '폭행을 당하다'처럼 피해를 말할 때도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: He was assaulted on the road at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피해를 입은 사람 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the victim's point of view.

phrases.example: 어제 우리 동네에서 폭행 사건이 있었어요.
phrases.en: There was an assault case in our neighborhood yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 명사 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase often used in the news.

phrases.en: You must not hit your friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '폭행하다'보다 이 말을 훨씬 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation this is used much more often than 'to assault'.

explain_en: 폭행하다 is used for hitting or harming a person by force. It's a stiff word common in news and legal talk, so in everyday conversation 때리다 sounds more natural. For the victim's side, people often say 폭행을 당하다.

examples.en: Abusing a child is punished by law.
A person who abused animals appeared on the news.
If a parent abuses a child, you have to report it.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 직원을 학대한다는 소문이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a rumor that the company mistreats its employees.

examples.ko: 누구도 약한 사람을 학대해서는 안 돼요.
examples.en: No one should mistreat a weaker person.
I saw a video of someone abusing a cat and reported it.

explain: 힘이 약한 사람이나 동물에게 몸과 마음의 상처를 주는 심각한 일에 써요. 가볍게 놀리는 정도에는 안 써요. 당한 쪽은 '학대를 당하다', '학대받다'라고 해요. '괴롭히다'보다 훨씬 무겁고 법과 뉴스에 자주 나오는 말이에요.

phrases.en: That child was abused for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학대받은 쪽에서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the person who suffered the abuse.

phrases.en: You must not abuse animals.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약한 동물에게 해를 주는 일을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for harming weak animals.

phrases.en: Child abuse must be reported.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스와 법에서 자주 나오는 명사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase common in news and law.

explain_en: It refers to serious harm done to the body or mind of someone weaker, such as a child or an animal, and is not used for light teasing. The victim is described as 학대를 당하다 or 학대받다. It is much heavier than 괴롭히다 (to bother, bully) and often appears in law and the news.

en: to be liberated; to be set free; to be emancipated

examples.en: The exam is over, so I'm free from studying.
When I leave work, I feel freed from it.
I'm free from a long worry, so I feel at ease.
Korea was liberated from Japan in 1945.

examples.ko: 집안일에서 해방될 수 있는 방법이 없을까요?
examples.en: Isn't there a way to get free from housework?
The liberated people came out to the streets and rejoiced.

explain: 일상에서는 '벗어나다', '자유로워지다'를 쓰고, '해방되다'는 힘들던 일이나 억압에서 벗어난 기쁨을 크게 말할 때 써요. 역사 이야기에서는 1945년 광복을 '해방'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I finally got free from the hard work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, more everyday word.

phrases.en: It's vacation, so my body and mind feel free.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얽매인 것이 없어져 편안해진 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the relaxed state of no longer being tied down.

phrases.en: With the exams over, I feel a sense of liberation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해방'에 '감'을 붙여 그 기분을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 감 to 해방 names that feeling.

explain_en: In daily life '벗어나다' or '자유로워지다' fit; '해방되다' stresses the joy of escaping something hard or oppressive. In history, the 1945 liberation is also called '해방'.

examples.en: Church members donated for the church's construction.
I give part of my salary as an offering every month.
I haven't decided yet how much to give.
Many people give offerings out of gratitude.
After giving the offering, I felt at ease.
They set up a scholarship with the money my friend donated.

explain: '기부하다'와 비슷하지만 종교 단체에 돈을 낼 때 주로 써요. 일반 단체나 학교에 돈을 낼 때는 '기부하다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I went to church for the first time and gave an offering.
phrases.nuance_ko: '헌금하다'를 명사로 풀어 쓴 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form that spells out 헌금하다 with the noun.

phrases.en: I want to donate for the new building.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이나 마음을 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form used to express a wish or intention.

phrases.en: I donated books to the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종교 단체가 아닌 곳에 돈이나 물건을 줄 때는 이 말이 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural when giving money or goods to places that aren't religious groups.

explain_en: It is similar to '기부하다', but it is mainly used for giving money to a religious organization. For ordinary organizations or schools, '기부하다' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 이 행동은 형법에 따라 처벌받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: This act can be punished under the criminal law.
I have a friend who studies criminal law at university.

examples.ko: 형법은 어떤 행동이 범죄인지 정해 놓은 법이에요.
examples.en: Criminal law is the law that sets which acts count as crimes.
The revised criminal law takes effect next month.
Please explain the difference between criminal law and civil law.

examples.ko: 변호사 시험에 형법 문제가 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Many criminal law questions came up on the bar exam.

explain: 형법은 범죄와 벌을 다루고, 민법은 사람 사이의 재산·가족 문제를 다뤄요. 그래서 도둑질이나 폭행은 형법 이야기고, 계약이나 이혼은 민법 이야기예요. 법 이름이라 '형법 제○조'처럼 숫자와 함께 자주 써요.

phrases.en: If you break the criminal law, you can be punished.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법을 지키지 않았다는 뜻으로 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing meaning not obeying the law.

phrases.en: This kind of behavior is a crime under criminal law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형법의 기준으로 볼 때라는 뜻으로 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain that something is so by the standard of criminal law.

phrases.en: Article 250 of the Criminal Act is the provision on murder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법 조문을 말할 때 숫자와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with a number when citing a statute.

explain_en: The criminal law deals with crimes and punishment, while the civil law deals with property and family matters between people. So theft and assault are criminal law, while contracts and divorce are civil law. As a law's name it often appears with numbers, as in '형법 제○조'.

examples.en: An employee embezzled company money.

examples.ko: 그는 모임 회비를 횡령해서 모두를 놀라게 했어요.
examples.en: He embezzled the club dues and shocked everyone.

examples.ko: 돈을 횡령하면 법에 따라 벌을 받아요.
examples.en: If you embezzle money, you are punished by law.
The person who tried to embezzle money was found out early.

examples.ko: 경리가 몰래 횡령하고 있었다는 사실이 밝혀졌어요.
examples.en: It came out that the accountant had been secretly embezzling.

examples.ko: 공금을 횡령할 생각은 절대 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must never think of embezzling public funds.

explain: '공금을 횡령하다', '돈을 횡령하다'처럼 목적어에 돈이나 물건이 와요. 맡은 것을 쓰는 거라서 '훔치다'와 다르고, 뉴스에서는 '횡령 혐의'로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: That employee embezzled public funds and was fired.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목적어로 돈이 올 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with money as the object.

phrases.en: He returned all the money he had embezzled.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여서 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-ㄴ' lets the verb describe the noun that follows.

phrases.example: 남이 맡긴 돈을 횡령하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You must not embezzle money that someone else entrusted to you.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙이나 도덕을 말할 때 쓰는 금지 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A prohibition form used for rules or morals.

explain_en: The object is money or goods, as in '공금을 횡령하다' (embezzle public funds). Because the money was entrusted to you, it differs from '훔치다' (steal), and in the news it often appears as '횡령 혐의' (suspicion of embezzlement).

examples.en: Someone damaged the trees in the park.
If you damage a cultural property, you must pay a fine.
A false rumor damaged his reputation.
I oppose development that damages nature.
I damaged a library book and had to pay for it.
We must be careful not to damage trust.

explain: '망가뜨리다'보다 딱딱하고, 문화재, 자연, 명예, 신뢰처럼 소중한 것을 상하게 할 때 써요. 컵이나 장난감이 부서지는 일에는 어울리지 않아요. 뉴스와 법 이야기에서 '명예 훼손', '문화재 훼손'처럼 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The old painting was damaged by the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소중한 것이 상한 결과를 말하는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, stating that something valuable has been damaged.

phrases.example: 거짓말로 남의 명예를 훼손하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You must not harm someone's reputation with lies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 좋은 평판을 해친다는 뜻으로 뉴스와 법에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means harming a person's good reputation and is common in news and law.

phrases.en: Please don't damage the mural in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 소중한 것을 상하게 하지 말라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in notices to ask people not to damage something valuable.

explain_en: Stiffer than 망가뜨리다 (break, ruin), it is used for harming valuable things such as cultural property, nature, reputation or trust. It doesn't suit a broken cup or toy. In the news you will see 명예 훼손 (defamation) and 문화재 훼손 (damage to cultural property).
